entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sabu called Kem was High Priest of Ptah, probably during the reign of Pepi I.

Kem's significance lies in his role as a chief craftsman and priest of the Egyptian sun god Ptah, a position that reflects the importance of craftsmanship and divine worship in ancient Egyptian society.

As High Priest, Kem played a crucial role in the festival of the Sun, a major religious event that brought together craftsmen, priests, and the royal family.

Kem's legacy extends to the transmission of Ptah's cult to subsequent generations, influencing the development of Egyptian religion and art.

He was also a key figure in the Sokar temple, a major center of worship and burial in ancient Egypt.

Sabu called Kem's story is one of a dedicated priest who, through his devotion to Ptah, played a vital role in the cultural and religious landscape of ancient Egypt.
